# NVIDIA B200 Pricing


Nathanael Chiang


September 29, 2026


3 min read


An NVIDIA B200 rents for $4.11 to $14.24 per GPU-hour on demand across the nine providers below. Beam's on-demand machine is the low end at $4.11 per hour. Other GPU clouds list $6.00 to $8.60, while AWS and Oracle sell only 8-GPU shapes at $14.24 and $14.00 per GPU. The median across 20 providers tracked by getdeploying is about $6.70.


## Key takeaways


- Beam's $4.11 machine is the cheapest on-demand B200 here. RunPod Community Cloud is next at $5.98.
- CoreWeave, AWS, Oracle and Hyperstack rent the B200 only as 8-GPU nodes.
- Preemptible capacity is far cheaper: Nebius starts at $0.99 per GPU-hour.


## B200 cloud prices per hour, by provider


Provider SKU On-demand $/GPU-hr Notes

Market median — $6.70 Across 20 providers with an on-demand price (getdeploying)


## How these prices were collected


Each figure is an on-demand list price per GPU-hour from the provider's own pricing page, with spot, preemptible and reserved rates excluded. We used single-GPU shapes where offered and divided 8-GPU node prices by eight.


- [Beam pricing page](https://www.beam.cloud/pricing)
- [Hyperstack GPU pricing page](https://www.hyperstack.cloud/gpu-pricing) , including reserved B200 rates
- [RunPod GPU pricing page](https://www.runpod.io/pricing)
- [Lambda instance pricing page](https://lambda.ai/pricing)
- [Nebius price list](https://nebius.com/prices) , including preemptible GPU rates
- [Spheron B200 rental page](https://www.spheron.network/gpu-rental/b200/)
- [CoreWeave pricing page](https://www.coreweave.com/pricing)
- [Oracle Cloud price list](https://www.oracle.com/cloud/price-list/) for the BM.GPU.B200.8 shape
- [AWS EC2 on-demand pricing page](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand/)
- [getdeploying B200 price tracker](https://getdeploying.com/gpus/nvidia-b200) for the market median


## Why B200 cloud prices vary so widely


The biggest split is between hyperscalers and GPU clouds. AWS and Oracle charge about twice the $6.00 to $8.60 most GPU clouds list, and both rent 8-GPU shapes only, at $113.93 and $112.00 per hour. CoreWeave also sells whole nodes, at $68.80 per hour. Shape matters within a provider too: Lambda charges $6.99 per GPU on one card and $6.69 on eight. Marketplace rates move with the host. Spheron's cheapest on-demand B200 is a host in Finland at $8.43, and its US Central listing is $9.36.


## Where to rent a B200 for less


Beam's $4.11 is the lowest on-demand B200 price in this data, with vCPU, RAM, and NVMe included. RunPod Community Cloud follows at $5.98, billed per second. Hyperstack ($6.00 on demand, $5.10 reserved) and Lambda both show as out of stock on getdeploying. The one rate below Beam's is preemptible: Nebius starts at $0.99 per GPU-hour, and those instances can be stopped at any time. CoreWeave spot ($4.26 per GPU) and Spheron spot ($4.42) both cost more than Beam on demand.


## What this means for your workload


A B200 pays off on compute-heavy work: training runs where time to result matters, and large-model inference in FP8 or FP4. Lambda, CoreWeave and Oracle list 180 GB of memory per GPU; Hyperstack lists 192 GB. For training across a full node, see our guide to[multi-GPU distributed training](https://www.beam.cloud/blog/multi-gpu-distributed-training) . If your model fits in 141 GB and isn't compute-bound, an[H200](https://www.beam.cloud/blog/nvidia-h200-pricing) costs about half as much on Beam, $2.09 against $4.11.


## FAQ


### How much does a B200 cost per hour?


On demand, it runs from $4.11 per GPU-hour on Beam to $14.24 on AWS, where you rent a full 8-GPU instance. Most GPU clouds charge $6.00 to $8.60.


### What's the cheapest way to rent a B200?


Beam's $4.11 on-demand machine is the lowest price we found, followed by RunPod Community Cloud at $5.98. If your job can handle interruptions, Nebius preemptible B200 starts at $0.99 per GPU-hour.


### B200 vs H200: which should I rent?


Rent the H200 if your model fits in 141 GB and hourly cost matters most; on Beam it costs $2.09 against $4.11. Rent the B200 for compute-heavy training or FP4 inference, where the newer Blackwell chip finishes sooner.
